snapshot.summary: Post and regularly update on its website the status of each capital project, including timelines, funding sources, delays, and cost overruns.
snapshot.quote: the department shall post on the website of the department, the status of each such capital project. Such information shall be updated on a triannual basis

snapshot.summary: Post on its website summary statistics on completed and pending capital projects, including completion times, funding changes, and delay reasons.
snapshot.quote: The department shall also post on its website the total number of capital projects that were completed during the most recent fiscal year, the average amount of time taken to complete such projects

snapshot.actor: the department of consumer and worker protection
snapshot.summary: Take measures necessary to implement the local law, including promulgating rules, before the law's effective date.
snapshot.quote: may take such measures as are necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date.

snapshot.actor: An agency or agencies designated by the mayor
snapshot.summary: Develop a pilot program to involve mental health professional candidates in student wellness clubs and mental health education in middle and high schools.
snapshot.quote: An agency or agencies designated by the mayor shall develop a pilot program to involve mental health professional candidates in student wellness clubs and mental health education in middle and high schools at the invitation of the principals of the schools that wish to participate.

snapshot.actor: the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to this subdivision
snapshot.summary: Make best efforts to recruit mental health professional candidates for voluntary participation in the pilot program.
snapshot.quote: Make best efforts to recruit mental health professional candidates for voluntary participation in such program;

snapshot.actor: the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to this subdivision
snapshot.summary: Make best efforts to develop partnerships with universities to recruit professional candidates for the pilot program.
snapshot.quote: Make best efforts to develop partnerships with universities to recruit professional candidates for voluntary participation in such program; and

snapshot.actor: the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to this subdivision
snapshot.summary: Facilitate discussions and workshops led by mental health professional candidates for middle and high school students on mental health topics.
snapshot.quote: Facilitate the leading of discussions and workshops by mental health professional candidates for middle and high school students on mental health topics, including but not limited to, mental health coping skills, recognizing signs of mental distress, and strategies for maintaining mental well-being.

snapshot.actor: The agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to this subdivision
snapshot.summary: Make best efforts to coordinate with the chancellor of the city school district to establish the pilot program within student wellness clubs.
snapshot.quote: The agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to this subdivision shall make best efforts to coordinate with the chancellor of the city school district to establish such program within student wellness clubs in middle and high schools.

snapshot.actor: the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to subdivision b
snapshot.summary: Commence the pilot program developed and established under subdivision b.
snapshot.deadline_text: no later than 1 year after the effective date of this local law
snapshot.quote: The pilot program developed and established under subdivision b of this section shall commence no later than 1 year after the effective date of this local law.

snapshot.actor: the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to subdivision b of this section
snapshot.summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council, and post on the agency's website, a report on the pilot program's implementation and outcomes.
snapshot.deadline_text: No later than 3 years after the effective date of this local law
snapshot.quote: No later than 3 years after the effective date of this local law, the agency or agencies designated by the mayor pursuant to subdivision b of this section, in coordination with the chancellor of the city school district, shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on the agency or agencies’ website, a report on the pilot program developed and established under subdivision b of this section.

snapshot.summary: Provide persons in custody with pending criminal proceedings access to evidence review technology to review evidence in their case.
snapshot.quote: The department shall provide any person in the care and custody of the department with a pending criminal proceeding access to evidence review technology for the purpose of enabling such person to review evidence that may be used in such proceeding, including audio, text, and visual materials.

snapshot.summary: Submit and post a report on the department's provision of access to evidence review technology, including feedback and recommendations.
snapshot.quote: No later than October 1, 2026, the board of correction shall submit to the mayor, the department, and the speaker of the council, and post on the board\u2019s website, a report about the department\u2019s provision of access to evidence review technology pursuant to this section.

snapshot.summary: Respond to the board of correction's report on evidence review technology, stating whether recommendations will be adopted and a timetable for implementation.
snapshot.deadline_text: no later than 30 days after submission to the department of such report
snapshot.quote: The department shall respond to the report no later than 30 days after submission to the department of such report.

snapshot.summary: Submit an additional annual report on the department's provision of access to evidence review technology.
snapshot.quote: No later than October 1, 2027, and no later than October 1 of each year thereafter, the board may submit an additional report in accordance with this subdivision.

snapshot.summary: Design signage describing transgender patients' rights and make it available to hospitals citywide.
snapshot.quote: The department shall design signs describing the rights of transgender patients and make such signs available to hospitals in the city.

snapshot.summary: Post information about transgender patients' rights on its website and make it available in designated citywide languages.
snapshot.quote: The department shall post information about the rights of transgender patients on its website and make such information available in the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101.

snapshot.summary: Coordinate with hospitals to identify services each offers to meet the specific needs of transgender individuals, including gender-affirming health care.
snapshot.quote: Coordinate with hospitals in the city to identify the services offered by each hospital to meet the specific needs of transgender individuals, including, but not limited to, gender-affirming health care;

snapshot.summary: Provide guidance to hospitals encouraging them to post in a conspicuous location a list of transgender-specific services offered.
snapshot.quote: Provide guidance to hospitals in the city encouraging such hospitals to post in a conspicuous location a list of any such services offered;

snapshot.summary: Coordinate with hospitals to update lists of transgender-specific services offered, as needed.
snapshot.quote: Coordinate with hospitals in the city to update the lists of such services offered by each hospital, as needed; and

snapshot.summary: Publish guidance and lists of transgender-specific hospital services on the department's website and the 311 citizen center website, in designated citywide languages.
snapshot.quote: Publish such guidance and such lists of services on the department’s website and on the 311 citizen center website. Such guidance shall be published in the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101.

snapshot.summary: Collaborate with city agencies to analyze data, promote data-driven policymaking, and support agencies in developing their own analytics strategies.
snapshot.quote: Collaborate with agencies to: (i) analyze data, promote data-driven policy making, decision making, conduct research and analysis to best fulfill agencies’ respective missions, and support agencies in developing strategies to conduct their own analytics based on such data

snapshot.summary: Collaborate with the department of information technology and telecommunications and other mayoral offices to facilitate data sharing and citywide analytics of public and non-public data.
snapshot.quote: Collaborate with the department of information technology and telecommunications, mayor’s office of operations, the mayor’s office for economic opportunity, the mayor’s office of information privacy, and other relevant offices in order to: (i) facilitate data sharing between city agencies and citywide analytics of publicly and non-publicly available data

snapshot.summary: Advise city agencies on data analytics and data integration best practices when sharing data, procuring data systems, and hiring or training analytics staff.
snapshot.quote: Advise agencies on data analytics and data integration strategy best practices when sharing data, procuring new data systems, and hiring or training analytics staff;

snapshot.summary: Maintain a public open analytics library sharing source code for data analytics projects on the office's website.
snapshot.quote: Maintain an open analytics library that shall allow the office of data analytics to share the source code for data analytics projects to increase awareness of the way city agencies use data and develop analytical tools.

snapshot.summary: Serve as the designated point of contact for outside partners contributing to or using public data sets.
snapshot.quote: Serve as the designated point of contact for outside partners contributing to or using public data sets;

snapshot.summary: Work with the department of information technology and telecommunications and other agencies to implement the open data law and ensure accessibility of public data sets.
snapshot.quote: Work with department of information technology and telecommunications, and other agencies as appropriate, to implement the city’s open data law, assist agency open data coordinators in ensuring compliance by their agencies with requirements regarding accessibility to public data sets

snapshot.summary: Guide training of agency staff, community boards, and the public on the open data web portal, and develop and implement an open data public education strategy.
snapshot.quote: Guide the training of agency staff, community boards and members of the public on the use of the web portal required by section 23-502 of the administrative code, and develop and implement an open data public education strategy.

snapshot.summary: Possess additional powers that the mayor or the head of the department where the office is established may choose to assign.
snapshot.quote: The director shall possess such powers, in addition to any powers vested in him or her pursuant to any other provision of law that may be assigned by the mayor or head of such department wherein the office has been established.

snapshot.summary: Require that developers receiving city financial assistance for a housing development project set aside at least 15 percent of income-restricted rental units for homeless individuals and families.
snapshot.quote: The department shall require that any developer who receives city financial assistance for a housing development project sets aside for homeless individuals and families at least 15 percent of the number of dwelling units offered for rent

snapshot.summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and the speaker of the council specifying data on set-aside units in housing development and preservation projects receiving city financial assistance.
snapshot.deadline_text: By no later than September 30, 2021, and by September 30 in each year thereafter
snapshot.quote: By no later than September 30, 2021, and by September 30 in each year thereafter, the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report specifying the following data

snapshot.summary: Check each contribution reported by a principal committee against the doing business database and notify the principal committee within the specified timeframe if a contribution exceeds doing business contribution limitations.
snapshot.deadline_text: within twenty days of the reporting of such contribution
snapshot.quote: The board shall check each contribution against the doing business database and shall notify the principal committee within twenty days of the reporting of such contribution if a contribution exceeding the doing business contribution limitation set forth in subdivision 1-a of section 3-703 is subject to such limitations

snapshot.summary: Provide notification to the principal or authorized committee within three business days of the reporting of a contribution in the six weeks preceding a covered election if the contribution exceeds doing business contribution limitations.
snapshot.deadline_text: within three business days of the reporting of such contribution to the board
snapshot.quote: Notwithstanding any provision in this subdivision, in the six weeks preceding the covered election the board shall provide such notification to the principal or authorized committee within three business days of the reporting of such contribution to the board

snapshot.summary: Provide a public particularized explanation when a surveillance technology product listed in more than one impact and use policy is claimed not to be distinct.
snapshot.quote: If a surveillance technology product identified pursuant to paragraph 3 of this subdivision is included in more than one impact and use policy, the department shall provide a public particularized explanation of why the department takes the position that such product is not a distinct surveillance technology that requires the proposal of a new impact and use policy.

snapshot.summary: Update an existing impact and use policy to describe a new but not distinct surveillance technology that differs in form or manufacturer.
snapshot.quote: The department shall update an existing impact and use policy to describe a new, but not distinct, surveillance technology, which has the same function but substantially differs in form or has a different manufacturer or product name.

snapshot.actor: a surveillance technology impact and use policy
snapshot.summary: Identify the manufacturer and product name, including the specific capability and component, of each surveillance technology addressed by a policy.
snapshot.quote: A surveillance technology impact and use policy shall identify the manufacturer and product name of each surveillance technology that is addressed by the impact and use policy, including the specific capability and component of the surveillance technology that is addressed by such policy if such product is listed in more than one such policy

snapshot.summary: Withhold public disclosure of a surveillance technology's manufacturer or product name when disclosure would endanger safety or interfere with an investigation.
snapshot.quote: the department shall not publicly disclose such manufacturer or product name, or both, to the extent such disclosure would pose such a risk

snapshot.summary: Provide a public particularized explanation of why disclosing a manufacturer or product name would endanger safety or interfere with an investigation.
snapshot.quote: the department shall provide a public particularized explanation, specific to the relevant surveillance technology, of why such disclosure would endanger the safety of the public or officers or interfere with an active investigation

snapshot.summary: Disclose manufacturer or product names of surveillance technology to the commissioner of investigation even when withheld from the public.
snapshot.quote: Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to permit the department to withhold disclosure of manufacturers or product names from the commissioner of investigation.

snapshot.summary: Create an internal tracking system to document instances of external data sharing and government agency access to surveillance technology data.
snapshot.deadline_text: Within 270 days of the effective date of the local law that added this subdivision
snapshot.quote: Within 270 days of the effective date of the local law that added this subdivision, the department shall create an internal tracking system that complies with this subdivision.

snapshot.summary: Document each instance in which the department provides an external entity with data collected using surveillance technology, including entity name and date.
snapshot.quote: Such tracking system shall document each instance in which the department provides an external entity with data collected by the department using a surveillance technology, including the name of the entity and the date that such data was provided.

snapshot.summary: Document each instance in which the department provides surveillance technology data to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement or Customs and Border Protection.
snapshot.quote: such system shall document each instance in which the department provides data to United States immigration and customs enforcement and United States customs and border protection, except data that is disclosed for the purposes of furthering a criminal investigation to any task force

snapshot.summary: Develop an internal tracking system listing each government agency with direct access to surveillance technology data, the extent, and the dates of such access.
snapshot.quote: the department shall develop an internal tracking system listing each local, state, or federal government agency that has direct access to data collected by the department using surveillance technology and the extent of the data to which the agency has direct access and for which dates the agency has direct access.

snapshot.summary: Develop a policy governing when local, state, or federal government agencies may access surveillance technology data collected by the department.
snapshot.quote: The department shall develop a policy regarding the circumstances under which any local, state, or federal government agency has access to data collected by the department using surveillance technology.

snapshot.summary: Conduct a review of evidence of physical safety hazards posed by surveillance technologies used by the department and include findings in its impact and use policies.
snapshot.deadline_text: Within 270 days of the local law that added this section and annually thereafter
snapshot.quote: Within 270 days of the local law that added this section and annually thereafter, the department shall conduct a review of evidence of physical safety hazards posed by surveillance technologies used by the department, including but not limited to evaluations by experts in the field, and shall include any identified physical hazards in the surveillance technology impact and use policy.

snapshot.actor: the New York city police department
snapshot.summary: Update and publish new surveillance technology impact and use policies to bring existing policies into compliance with this local law.
snapshot.deadline_text: within 270 days of the effective date of this local law
snapshot.quote: within 270 days of the effective date of this local law, the New York city police department shall update and publish new surveillance technology impact and use policies to bring existing impact and use policies into compliance with this local law

snapshot.summary: State, as part of the section 803 audit, whether any manufacturer or product name was improperly withheld.
snapshot.quote: As part of the audit pursuant to section 803 of the New York city charter, the commissioner of investigation may state whether any manufacturer or product name was improperly withheld.

snapshot.summary: Consolidate the intergovernmental data-sharing rules into a single policy covering all agencies, while noting any differing standards.
snapshot.quote: The department may develop one policy for all such data for all local, state, or federal government agencies, provided that, to the extent that certain categories of data or certain local, state, or federal government agencies receive data under different standards or in different circumstances, such differences shall be noted.

snapshot.summary: Prepare a recurring urban agriculture report addressing resources, classification of uses, healthy food access, resiliency integration, and youth education, and submit it to the mayor and council speaker and post it online.
snapshot.deadline_text: No later than October 1, 2023, and no later than October 1 of every fifth year thereafter
snapshot.quote: No later than October 1, 2023, and no later than October 1 of every fifth year thereafter, prepare an urban agriculture report, in cooperation with relevant agencies and stakeholders, including but not limited to food policy educators, representatives from community gardens and urban farming businesses.

snapshot.summary: Provide an annual update to the mayor and council speaker, posted on the city's website, reporting progress on recommendations from the most recent urban agriculture report.
snapshot.deadline_text: The first such update shall be completed no later than October 1, 2024.
snapshot.quote: Update the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post on the city’s website, an annual accounting of the progress made on the recommendations, initiatives and priorities identified in the most recent report prepared pursuant to paragraph 5 of this subdivision.

snapshot.summary: Require proof of an inspector's qualifications on any gas piping inspection report and certification.
snapshot.quote: The department shall require proof of such qualifications on any report and certification as required under section 28-318.3.3

snapshot.summary: Appoint annually each member of the plumbing and fire suppression piping contractor license board.
snapshot.quote: The commissioner shall appoint annually and may remove at the commissioner’s discretion each member of a plumbing and fire suppression piping contractor license board

snapshot.summary: Keep minutes of its proceedings and records of its investigations.
snapshot.quote: the board shall keep minutes of its proceedings and records of its investigations.

snapshot.summary: Remove any member of the plumbing and fire suppression piping contractor license board.
snapshot.quote: The commissioner may remove any member of the license board and shall fill any vacancy therein.

snapshot.summary: Request that the commissioner appoint duly authorized representatives to conduct investigations and other activities for the board.
snapshot.quote: The board may request the commissioner to appoint duly authorized representatives to conduct investigations and other activities incidental to the functions of the license board.

snapshot.summary: Promulgate rules to facilitate and enforce the added sugar notification requirements of this section.
snapshot.quote: The department shall promulgate rules for the facilitation and enforcement of this section.

snapshot.summary: Take all measures necessary to implement this local law, including promulgating implementing rules, before the law's effective date.
snapshot.quote: the commissioner shall take such measures as are necessary for its implementation, including the promulgation of rules, prior to such effective date

snapshot.summary: Furnish pet shops with a form for their required monthly reporting of all dogs sold and adopted, including license application status.
snapshot.quote: report to the department on a form furnished by the department all dogs which have been sold and adopted

snapshot.summary: Authorize the department to require pet shops to submit their sterilization records, veterinarian letters, and certificates by electronic means.
snapshot.quote: The department may require that such documents be submitted by electronic means.

snapshot.summary: Specify the manner in which pet shops and animal rescue groups must forward completed dog license applications and fees to the department.
snapshot.quote: Such pet shop or animal rescue group shall forward such completed application and license fees to the department in such manner as may be specified by the department.

snapshot.summary: Determine the form of proof required to establish that a dog purchaser or adopter resides outside the city for purposes of the licensing exemption.
snapshot.quote: proof in a form determined by the department that the purchaser or adopter resides outside the city
